# 05 — Bridge Architecture: C# RynthAi ⇄ Browser holtburger-web

## 0. TL;DR

- **Recommendation: option (b)** — a dedicated WebSocket side-channel, page dials *out* to a small WS server hosted inside the C# RynthAi process. **Reject (a)** CDP (per-call latency × 150 blows every tick budget) and **(c)** wsbridge (a stateless opaque AC-packet pipe on the *server* side with zero visibility into the browser's decoded game state — it is the wrong layer).
- **The load-bearing idea:** the 150 per-tick `TryGet*` polls must **never touch the wire**. The in-page shim composes **one batched snapshot per tick** from wasm getters + `entityMap` + the event stream, sends it as a single WS frame; the C# side caches it and answers all 150 synchronous `RynthCoreHost.TryGet*` calls from that cache. This is what dissolves the poll-vs-async inversion (§4).
- Actions stay fire-and-forget (one WS message each), mirroring both `RynthCoreHost`'s fire-and-forget contract and the wasm `cmd_tx.unbounded_send` pattern. Events ride a second, push channel sourced from `SessionHandle::poll_events`.

---

## 1. The real call surface: `RynthCoreHost.cs` classified by frequency

`RynthCoreHost` (`/home/wbterminal/ac-refs/rynthcore/src/RynthCore.PluginSdk/RynthCoreHost.cs`) is `ABI v66` (`RynthCoreHost.cs:8`), a poll-style seam: `TryGet*(out …)` synchronous reads returning `bool` + fire-and-forget action methods returning `bool` "delivered". Every method is capability-guarded by a matching `Has*` property (`.cs:23-119`), and version-gated methods AND `_api.<Fn> != IntPtr.Zero` (e.g. `HasGiveObjectTo => _api.Version >= 62 && …`, `.cs:114`).

The tick that drives it: `PluginManager.ProcessPendingActions(...)` (drains engine→plugin event queues) then `PluginManager.TickAll()` (calls each plugin's `OnTick`), run from **both** the headless Decal-coexistence pump (`RynthCore.Engine/EntryPoint.cs:869-877`) and the per-frame ImGui pump (`EngineFrameController.cs:428-430`). RynthAi's entry is `RynthAiPlugin.cs:874 OnTick()`.

Static call-site frequency across the whole RynthAi plugin (75 files; measured with `rg -oI 'Host\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+' | sort | uniq -c`): **374 `Host.*` call sites** total. Top reads: `TryGetPlayerPose ×15`, `TryGetObjectName ×14`, `UseObject ×13`, `GetPlayerId ×9`, `GetBusyState ×5`, `TryGetObjectPosition ×5`, `TryGetObjectIntProperty ×5`.

| Frequency class | Cadence | Representative host calls (file:line in `RynthCoreHost.cs`) | Bridge treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Per-tick poll** (fires every `OnTick`, must be zero-latency) | 60 Hz (per-frame) / ~20 Hz (headless pump) | `TryGetPlayerPose` :523, `TryGetPlayerHeading` :349, `TryGetCurCoords` :424, `GetPlayerId` :396, `GetBusyState` :632, `GetCastBusyState` :652 / `CanCastNow` :663, `GetUseDoneSeq` :676, `TryGetPlayerVitals` :705, `TryGetTargetVitals` :741, `GetCurrentCombatMode` :161, `GetSelectedItemId` :382, `IsPortaling` :562, `IsPlayerReady` :1263, `GetServerTime` :1007, `GetVitae` :568 | **Snapshot fields** — composed in-page, one frame/tick, answered from C# cache. |
| **Per-decision read** (bounded; on target-select / appraisal / loot pass, not every tick) | event-driven, 1–30 objs | `TryGetObjectName` :682, `TryGetObjectPosition` :927, `TryGetObjectWcid` :594, `ObjectIsAttackable` :837, `TryGetObjectIntProperty` :791, `…BoolProperty` :821, `…DoubleProperty` :1210, `…QuadProperty` :1198, `…StringProperty` :1222, `…DataIdProperty` :809, `GetObjectSpellIds` :1043, `ReadObjectEnchantments` :1014, `TryGetObjectSkill` :843, `TryGetItemType` :779, `HasAppraisalData` :612, `GetContainerContents` :1280, `GetNumContainedItems` :410 | **Per-entity block in snapshot** for nearby/selected objects; **on-demand request/response** (§2 `objGet`) for cold objects, gated by `RequestId` :735. |
| **Rare action** (fire-and-forget, returns bool "delivered") | event-driven, ≪1 Hz | `CastSpell` :773, `MeleeAttack` :195, `MissileAttack` :201, `ChangeCombatMode` :154, `CancelAttack` :183, `UseObject` :439, `UseObjectOn` :445, `MoveItemExternal` :457, `MoveItemInternal` :463, `GiveObjectTo` :501, `SelectItem` :370, `SetMotion` :331, `StopCompletely` :337, `TurnToHeading` :343, `Jump`/`DoJump` :257, `WriteToChat` :507, `InvokeChatParser` :1154, `RequestId` :735, `QueryHealth` :189, `Salvage*` :169-181 | **One WS action message each.** Return `true` optimistically on enqueue (matches wasm `cmd_tx` semantics). |
| **Session-static** (read once / rarely) | once | `Version` :17, `TryGetAccountName` :574, `TryGetWorldName` :584, `ReadKnownSpells` :985, `TryGetPlayerBaseVitals` :1184 | **Handshake / capability block.** |
| **Unportable islands** (do not bridge) | — | `ImGuiContext`/`D3DDevice`/`GameHwnd` :18-20, `Nav3D*` :1097-1150, `WorldToScreen` :1068, `SetRadarSuppressed` :302, `SetFpsLimit` :1271 | Stub `Has*→false`; RynthAi's 344 `Has*` guards degrade gracefully (established fact). |

The design implication is stark: **the per-tick poll class is the only one with a hard latency budget**, and it is a *fixed, enumerable set* (~16 fields + a small selected-target block). Everything else is event-paced. So the bridge only has to make ~16 fields cheap — not 150 arbitrary round-trips.

## 2. Prior art: `k1_drive_combat.cjs` (Playwright/CDP)

`apps/holtburger-web/k1_drive_combat.cjs` is a 377-line Playwright script that `chromium.connectOverCDP("http://127.0.0.1:9223")` (`:49`), then drives the page entirely through `page.evaluate()`:

**What it does well:**
- Zero page modification — attaches to a live Chrome over CDP, reuses the existing tab (`:52-56`). No shim to ship.
- Reads exactly the JS globals this integration would target: `window.__sessionHandle.getLocalPlayerPose()` (`:207`), `window.entityMap` walk (`:242-264`), `window.getLocalPlayerGuid()`, `window.__getCurrentStanceLow/Label()` (`:216-221`), and drives actions via `window.__sessionHandle.sendChat / toggleCombatMode / attack` (`:191, :226, :322-327`).
- Subscribes to the **event bus** for combat feedback: `window.__pluginClient.events.on("damageDealt"|"attackDone"|…)` (`:302-316`) — proving the event-stream channel (§5) already exists in-page.
- Correlates browser state against the server-side ACE log tail (`:35-45, :330-339`).

**Where it falls over at 150-call scale:**
- **Every read is a full CDP `Runtime.evaluate` round-trip.** The whole script issues **~10 evaluates across an entire multi-second run**. It never polls per-tick. A RynthAi brain needs the per-tick set (§1) at 20–60 Hz.
- **Serialization + main-thread contention.** Each `evaluate` serializes a JS source string over the CDP WebSocket, waits for Chrome's main thread to run it (queued *behind* the three.js rAF frame), then JSON-serializes the result back. Under render load that's one-to-several frames of tail latency. `k1` tolerates this by `sleep()`-ing seconds between steps (`:197, :228, :329`); a live brain cannot.
- **No batching primitive.** Playwright evaluates are sequential per execution context; 150 reads = 150 serialized round-trips funneled through one CDP pipe.
- **Cache-bust / lifecycle scaffolding** (`:59-98`) is smoke-test glue, not a control channel.

**Verdict:** excellent as a scripted validation harness and as the *inventory of exactly which globals to read*; unusable as the transport for a 20–60 Hz, 150-call brain.

## 3. Transport evaluation (modeled latencies)

Latencies below are **reasoned from mechanism cost on loopback**, not benchmarked on this box — labeled estimates. The relevant unit is *per-tick wall-clock*, against a 16.6 ms (60 Hz) / 50 ms (20 Hz headless) budget.

| Option | Mechanism | Per-op RTT (loopback, modeled) | Per-tick cost @150 reads | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **(a) CDP / Playwright `evaluate`** | `Runtime.evaluate` over DevTools WS; source-string in, JSON out; runs on page main thread | p50 **~1–4 ms** idle; **p99 16–50 ms** under rAF load (queues behind frame) | **naive:** 150 × 2–4 ms = **300–600 ms** (sequential); even one batched evaluate returning all 150 fields = 1 RTT but still 2–50 ms + main-thread stall | ❌ Latency floor is a frame; tail is multiple frames. Fine for `k1`-style scripting only. |
| **(b) Dedicated WS side-channel + in-page shim** ⭐ | Page dials `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>` to a WS server inside the C# host; **one snapshot frame/tick** composed in-page; actions are WS messages back | **snapshot compose in-page ~0.1–0.5 ms** (one main-thread pass over RefCell shadows + `entityMap`) + **WS send ~0.05–0.3 ms one-way** on loopback TCP | **~0.5–1 ms/tick** (150 reads become **0-wire** C# cache hits) + 1 frame | ✅ Snapshot is push, not pull; polls never cross the wire. |
| **(c) Piggyback `holtburger-wsbridge`** | Reuse the existing WS↔UDP relay process | n/a | n/a | ❌ Wrong layer — see below. |

### Why (c) is the wrong layer (grounded in the source)

`holtburger-wsbridge` is a **stateless, opaque AC-packet byte pipe on the server side**, in front of ACE:
- It never parses AC bytes: "Neither binary parses AC bytes, does crypto, or knows about sessions, players, or login state. Both are pipes" (`ARCHITECTURE.md:23`), "Bytes are opaque end-to-end" (`:160`).
- Its frames are `[port:u16 BE][ac_packet_bytes]` (`frame.rs:23-56`); post-handshake it **rejects any non-binary frame** — "post-handshake non-binary ws frame is not part of the protocol" (`bridge.rs:253-257`) — and rejects any port not on the ACE login/world allowlist (`bridge.rs:227-234`).
- It has "no per-connection state beyond the two sockets" (`ARCHITECTURE.md:78`), and lives between the *browser* and *ACE*, i.e. it sees **encrypted, undecoded AC UDP packets** — not the decoded game state the brain needs.

The decoded game state (`entityMap`, vitals, pose, busy-gate) exists **only in the browser, after `holtburger-session` decodes it inside the wasm**. The bridge is physically on the other side of that decode. To broker a bot channel it would have to either (i) add an out-of-band control channel — **explicitly considered and rejected** in the design ("Out-of-band control channel … Rejected — the design doc explicitly wants a stateless bridge", `ARCHITECTURE.md:56`) — and *still* not have decoded state, or (ii) re-decode AC packets in C#, which is literally the **native RynthCoreHost path**, not the web path. Reject.

---

## 4. THE key design — per-tick batched snapshot composed in-page

This is the heart of the integration and the resolution of the poll-vs-async inversion.

### 4.1 The inversion, precisely

`RynthCoreHost.TryGetPlayerPose(out …)` **returns a value synchronously, now** (`.cs:523`). The browser cannot be read synchronously from C#: page state lives behind an async event loop / rAF; the wasm getters (`get_local_player_pose` → `*self.local_player_pose.borrow()`, `lib.rs:31268`) are only callable *on the page's main thread*. Bridging naively (one WS request/response per `TryGet*`) reintroduces per-call latency × 150 — the very thing that killed option (a).

### 4.2 The fix: snapshot-cache on the C# side, push from the page

```
  BROWSER (page main thread)                     C# RynthAi process
  ┌───────────────────────────────┐              ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
  │ in-page bot shim               │  snapshot    │ WebHostBridge (WS server)         │
  │  rAF/interval @ tickHz:        │  frame ───▶  │  onMessage: swap latest snapshot  │
  │   compose SnapshotV1 from       │  (1/tick)    │   into WebHostSnapshot (volatile) │
  │   wasm getters + entityMap +    │              │                                   │
  │   drained events               │  ◀── action   │ RynthCoreHost.TryGetPlayerPose ─┐ │
  │  onWSMessage(action): apply     │  frame       │   reads WebHostSnapshot.Pose ←──┘ │
  │   via __sessionHandle.<cmd>()   │  (rare)      │   (SYNC, 0-wire) → returns true   │
  └───────────────────────────────┘              └──────────────────────────────────┘
```

- The page **pushes** one `SnapshotV1` frame per tick. The C# `WebHostBridge` stores it (last-writer-wins, `Volatile`/`Interlocked` swap).
- `RynthCoreHost.TryGet*` are reimplemented to read the **cached snapshot** — synchronous, zero-wire, last-known value. This *is* AC client semantics anyway: the native host also returns last-observed values from client memory.
- The 150 per-tick polls collapse to **150 synchronous C# field reads against one cached struct**; the wire carries **1 snapshot frame + N rare action frames** per tick.
- The RynthAi tick (`OnTick`) runs on the C# pump thread; snapshot arrival is decoupled from it. If a snapshot is stale (page stalled / tab-occluded), C# returns the last one and can expose staleness (see `snapSeq`/`snapAgeMs`) so the brain can throttle — exactly how RynthAi already tolerates a missing cast-gate ("callers should pair it with their own throttle", `RynthCoreHost.cs:648-651`).

### 4.3 SnapshotV1 fields (derived from the per-tick poll set §1)

Composed in-page each tick. Fields map 1:1 to the per-tick host reads; sources cited.

| Snapshot field | Source in page | Feeds host call |
|---|---|---|
| `seq`, `tMs`, `serverTimeMs` | shim counter, `performance.now()`, wasm server-clock | freshness; `GetServerTime` :1007 |
| `player{objCellId,x,y,z,heading,landblockId,onGround}` | `getLocalPlayerPose()` → `LocalPlayerPose{x,y,z,heading,landblock_id,…}` (`lib.rs:31268`, struct `:28849`) | `TryGetPlayerPose` :523, `TryGetPlayerHeading` :349, `TryGetCurCoords` :424 |
| `playerId` | `getLocalPlayerGuid()` (JS global, `k1:220`) | `GetPlayerId` :396 |
| `vitals{h,hMax,s,sMax,m,mMax}` | world-state cache updated by kind=8/42/43/44 events (`api.js` taxonomy) | `TryGetPlayerVitals` :705 |
| `combatMode` | `__getCurrentStanceLow()` (`k1:216`) / stance-toggle state | `GetCurrentCombatMode` :161 |
| `busy`, `castBusy`, `useDoneSeq`, `playerReady`, `isPortaling` | wasm gate getters (need thin exports, §5.2) / recv-loop state | `GetBusyState` :632, `GetCastBusyState` :652, `GetUseDoneSeq` :676, `IsPlayerReady` :1263, `IsPortaling` :562 |
| `selectedGuid` | picking.js `setSelectedTarget` state (`k1:325`) | `GetSelectedItemId` :382 |
| `targetVitals{…}` | selected entity's `entityMap` entry / kind=54 EntityHealth (`index.html:7860`) | `TryGetTargetVitals` :741 |
| `nearby[]` — per-entity block: `{guid,wcid,name,x,y,z,heading,attackable,itemType,physicsState,healthFrac}` for the K nearest / on-screen objects | walk `window.entityMap` (`index.html:2974,3017`; `entities.js:3101,4228`), same walk as `k1:242-264` | Per-decision reads: `TryGetObjectName` :682, `…Position` :927, `…Wcid` :594, `ObjectIsAttackable` :837, `TryGetItemType` :779 |

Cold objects not in `nearby[]` (deep pack contents, un-appraised weenies) use an **on-demand `objGet` request/response** (§5.1), gated behind `RequestId` :735 — matching how RynthAi already appraises via `RequestId` + `HasAppraisalData` :612 before reading properties.

### 4.4 Event stream channel (separate from the snapshot)

Snapshot = level (current state). Events = edges (things that happened). The page already produces both:
- **`SessionHandle::poll_events() -> Vec<ClientEvent>`** (`lib.rs:29229`) — drained by JS every rAF (`index.html:5446 handle.poll_events()`), dispatched by `evt.kind` (`index.html:7015-8080`; kind=14 UseDone `:7964`, kind=54 EntityHealth `:7860`, kind=19 combat family) and re-emitted onto the bus `window.__pluginClient.events.emit(...)` (`index.html:2905`).
- `ClientEvent` JS fields: `kind`, `stringPayload`, `u32Payload`, `u32Payload2`, `f32Payload` (`lib.rs:22653-22685`).
- Separate `pollEntityUpdates` channel for spawns/removals/position (`lib.rs:29233`).

The shim forwards each drained `ClientEvent` (and spawn/remove EntityUpdates) as an **`event` WS frame**, pushed independently of the tick snapshot. On the C# side these drive `ProcessPendingActions`'s queues — the exact thing RynthAi's tick drains at `EntryPoint.cs:869` ("selected-target change, health update, enchantment add/remove, create/delete object, combat mode"). This is a clean 1:1: **ClientEvent kinds → engine→plugin event queues.**

## 5. Message schema sketch

Transport: WebSocket, **binary frames**, page → C#-host-hosted WS server (page dials out; no inbound socket to the browser). One JSON (or MessagePack/CBOR for density) envelope per frame. Framing = WS frame boundary (no length prefix needed).

### 5.1 Envelope + message types

```jsonc
// capability negotiation — first frame each direction (mirrors ABI v66 + Has*)
→ HELLO   { t:"hello", proto:1, hostAbi:66,             // page announces build
            caps:["pose","vitals","busy","castBusy","useDoneSeq","entityMap",
                  "objGet","attack","cast","moveItem","chat","combatMode", ...] }
← HELLOACK{ t:"helloack", proto:1, wantTickHz:20,        // C# picks tick rate,
            need:["pose","vitals","busy","selectedGuid","nearby"] }  //   subscribes to fields

// per-tick snapshot (page → host), one per tick, fire-and-forget push
→ SNAP    { t:"snap", seq:12345, tMs:…, player:{…}, playerId:…, vitals:{…},
            combatMode:2, busy:0, castBusy:0, useDoneSeq:41, selectedGuid:0x80..,
            targetVitals:{…}, nearby:[ {guid,wcid,name,x,y,z,attackable,…}, … ] }

// event stream (page → host), pushed as drained, out of band from snap
→ EVT     { t:"evt", kind:19, u32:0x80.., u32b:0, f32:0.5, s:"{json}" }  // ClientEvent 1:1

// action (host → page), rare, fire-and-forget; optional ack for delivered-bool
← ACT     { t:"act", id:88, fn:"attack", args:[0x80.., 2, 0.5] }
→ ACTACK  { id:88, ok:true }                              // optional; host returns true on enqueue

// on-demand cold read (host → page → host), request/response w/ id
← REQ     { t:"req", id:91, fn:"objGet", guid:0x50.., props:["name","intProp:25"] }
→ RES     { id:91, ok:true, v:{name:"Iron Key", "intProp:25":0} }
```

### 5.2 Capability negotiation mirroring `Has*` / ABI version

- `HELLO.hostAbi:66` mirrors `RynthCoreHost.CurrentApiVersion = 66` (`.cs:8`). The C# side refuses/degrades on mismatch exactly like the version gates at `.cs:106-119`.
- `HELLO.caps[]` is the wire analogue of the 100+ `Has*` properties (`.cs:23-119`). The reimplemented host sets `HasGetCastBusyState`, `HasGiveObjectTo`, etc. from whether the cap string is present — so RynthAi's **344 `Has*` guard sites** light up only what the page can actually serve, and the rest degrade gracefully (established fact).
- `HELLOACK.need[]` lets C# *subscribe* to only the snapshot fields the loaded brain reads, so the page doesn't compose/serialize `nearby[]` blocks nobody polls.
- Some per-tick fields need **thin new wasm getters** (they're currently only reachable via events, not synchronous shadows): `busyState`, `castBusy`, `useDoneSeq`, `isPortaling`, `playerVitals`. There is precedent for these synchronous shadow getters — `get_local_player_pose` :31268, `can_jump_now` :31291, `pursuit_status` :31321 all read `RefCell` shadows the recv loop keeps warm. Adding `getBusyState()/getPlayerVitals()` in the same pattern is the smallest page-side change.

## 6. The in-page shim: what JS it needs, which `SessionHandle` calls it wraps

The shim is a small ES module loaded by the page (guarded behind a URL flag, e.g. `?bot=1`, alongside the existing `?agent=1&autoLogin=1&nullRender=1&netDrainHz=N` bot-mode flags in `docs/url-flags.md`). It reuses the facade the page already builds: `createClient(handle)` → `window.__pluginClient` with `.player`/`.world`/`.events` (`plugins/api.js`; `index.html:5387`).

**Shim responsibilities:**
1. **Dial out** `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>` to the C# host's WS server after `window.__pluginClientReady` resolves (`index.html:1423`). Send `HELLO` with caps.
2. **Compose + push SNAP** every tick. Two cadence choices:
   - Piggyback the existing rAF drain loop (where `handle.poll_events()` already runs, `index.html:5446`) — free, render-coupled.
   - Or a wall-clock `setInterval` at `wantTickHz` (independent of rAF, survives tab-occlusion — same reasoning as the `sendKeepalive` 2.5 s interval, `lib.rs:31808-31827`). Recommended for headless `?nullRender=1` where rAF is throttled.
3. **Forward events.** In the same drain, wrap each `poll_events()` `ClientEvent` and `pollEntityUpdates()` entry into `EVT` frames. (Or subscribe on the bus `client.events.on(...)`, as `k1:302-316` does.)
4. **Apply actions.** On inbound `ACT`, dispatch to the wasm SessionHandle.

**`SessionHandle` / facade calls the shim wraps (all real, verified):**

| Host action (RynthCoreHost) | Shim calls (wasm `SessionHandle`, `lib.rs`) | Facade equiv (`api.js`) |
|---|---|---|
| `MeleeAttack` :195 | `attack(guid, height, power)` :32643 → `SessionCommand::TargetedMeleeAttack` | — |
| `MissileAttack` :201 | `missileAttack(...)` :32679 | — |
| `CancelAttack` :183 | `cancelAttack()` :32714 | — |
| `QueryHealth` :189 | `queryHealth(guid)` :32728 | — |
| `CastSpell` :773 | `castTargetedSpell(guid, spellId)` :32744 / `castUntargetedSpell(spellId)` :32766 | `castTargetedSpell` `api.js:474` |
| `ChangeCombatMode` :154 | `toggleCombatMode()` :32372 / `setCombatMode(mode)` :32390 | `toggleCombatMode` `api.js:443` |
| `UseObject` :439 / `UseObjectOn` :445 | `useObject(guid)` :32039 | `useObject` `api.js:425` |
| `MoveItemExternal` :457 | `moveItem/putItemInContainer(item,cont,slot)` :54436/:54456 | — |
| `WriteToChat`/`InvokeChatParser` :507/:1154 | `sendChat(msg)` :31796 / `sendTell` :31833 | `sendChat` `api.js:597` |
| `Jump`/`DoJump` :257 | `jump(power)` :32418 | — |
| — reads — | `getLocalPlayerPose()` :31268, `poll_events()` :29229, `pollEntityUpdates()` :29233, `entityMap` walk (`index.html:2974`) | `getLocalPlayerPose` `api.js:522`, `events` `api.js:740` |

Crucially, **the action side is already fire-and-forget on both ends**: every wasm action is `cmd_tx.unbounded_send(SessionCommand::X)` returning immediately (`lib.rs:32374, 32659, 32750, 54443`), which is exactly `RynthCoreHost`'s "returns true on enqueue" contract. No impedance mismatch on actions — only on reads, which §4 resolves.

## 7. Walking-skeleton milestone (2–3 days)

Goal: prove the snapshot-cache transport end-to-end with a *trivial* brain, before porting any of RynthAi's 51.5k lines. Scope deliberately excludes the real brain, the object property surface, and `RequestId` cold-reads.

**Day 1 — wire + snapshot (one field, one direction).**
- C# `WebHostBridge`: a `System.Net.WebSockets` server on `127.0.0.1:8091`; on connect, do `HELLO`/`HELLOACK` (proto 1, abi 66); store latest `SNAP` into a `volatile WebHostSnapshot`.
- In-page `bot-shim.js` (behind `?bot=1`): dial out, send `HELLO`, and on the existing rAF drain push a `SNAP` carrying just `{seq, player:getLocalPlayerPose()}` (`lib.rs:31268`).
- **Exit:** C# logs a live, advancing player pose at ~20 Hz with `snapAgeMs < 100`. Reuse `k1`'s login/spawn/`@telepoi holtburg` scaffolding (`k1:127-197`) to get in-world.

**Day 2 — synchronous host cache + one action round-trip.**
- Implement a **minimal `RynthCoreHost` shim class** whose `TryGetPlayerPose`/`GetPlayerId`/`GetBusyState` read `WebHostSnapshot` synchronously (0-wire), and whose `Has*` derive from `HELLO.caps`. Add the thin wasm getter `getBusyState()` if not already shadowed (pattern of `can_jump_now` :31291).
- Add `ACT` path: C# sends `{fn:"sendChat"}` → shim calls `__sessionHandle.sendChat` (`lib.rs:31796`). Then `{fn:"attack", args:[selectedGuid,2,0.5]}` → `attack` (`lib.rs:32643`), reusing `k1`'s target-pick (`k1:242-284`).
- **Exit:** a 30-line C# "toy brain" polling `host.TryGetPlayerPose()` + `host.GetBusyState()` each `OnTick`, that on a hostile in `nearby[]` fires `host.MeleeAttack(...)` — and the drudge takes damage (verify via `client.events.on("damageDealt")`, `k1:302-316`, and the ACE log tail, `k1:330-339`).

**Day 3 — event stream + capability/staleness hardening.**
- Forward `poll_events()` `ClientEvent`s as `EVT` frames (`lib.rs:29229`; fields :22653-22685); C# enqueues them into the `ProcessPendingActions`-style queues.
- Add `snapSeq`/`snapAgeMs` staleness gating so `TryGet*` can report stale; add `HELLOACK.need[]` field subscription; run under `?nullRender=1&netDrainHz=20` (pure-protocol bot mode, `docs/url-flags.md`) to confirm the wall-clock `setInterval` snapshot cadence survives with rendering off.
- **Exit:** toy brain reacts to a `kind=54 EntityHealth` event (`index.html:7860`) — e.g. stops attacking when target health hits 0 — proving snapshot (level) + events (edges) compose correctly, headless.

This skeleton exercises every structural seam that matters (sync cache over async push, fire-and-forget actions, capability negotiation, event stream) at the smallest possible surface, so porting the real RynthAi brain afterward is a matter of widening the field/cap set, not re-architecting the transport.

## Notes / caveats

- Latency figures in §3 are **modeled from mechanism cost** (loopback TCP/WS RTT, CDP `Runtime.evaluate` serialization + main-thread queueing), not benchmarked on this box. The *relative* ordering (WS ≪ CDP, and snapshot-push ≪ per-call-pull) is robust regardless of absolute numbers.
- `busyState`, `castBusy`, `useDoneSeq`, `playerVitals`, `isPortaling` currently reach JS via the **event stream**, not synchronous shadow getters; §5.2/Day-2 assume adding thin `RefCell`-shadow getters in the established `get_local_player_pose`/`can_jump_now` pattern. This is asserted from the getter/event split observed in `lib.rs`, not from an existing synchronous vitals export (none found: `rg 'js_name = getVitals|player_vitals'` → 0 hits).
- The unportable islands (Nav3D, WorldToScreen, D3D/ImGui handles, FellowshipTracker memory reads) are out of scope for the bridge — stub their `Has*` to false; RynthAi's guard sites already tolerate this (established fact).
